about.title: About Tire Calculator
about.description: The Tire Calculator analyzes how tire diameter changes affect vehicle speed, RPM, and overall driving characteristics. It is useful for tire upgrades, comparison checks, and reviewing speedometer differences. Understanding tire size impact helps compare clearance, handling, and fuel-economy tradeoffs when changing tire sizes.

faq.q: How does tire diameter affect speedometer accuracy?
faq.a: Larger tires make the speedometer read slower than actual speed, while smaller tires make it read faster. A 3% tire diameter increase typically causes 3% speedometer error. Our tire calculator helps estimate speedometer error for any tire size change.

faq.q: What's the maximum safe tire size increase?
faq.a: Generally, stay within 3% of original tire diameter to maintain speedometer accuracy and avoid clearance issues. Always check wheel well clearance, suspension travel, and brake line clearance before upgrading to larger tire sizes.

faq.q: How do larger tires affect fuel economy?
faq.a: Larger, heavier tires typically reduce fuel economy due to increased rolling resistance and rotational mass. The effect varies by tire weight, tread pattern, and vehicle type. Use our tire calculator to compare likely trade-offs before changing sizes.

faq.q: Will changing tire size affect my vehicle's performance?
faq.a: Yes, tire size changes significantly affect performance. Larger tires reduce acceleration but may improve top speed and handling. Smaller tires improve acceleration but may limit top speed. Our calculator helps you understand these trade-offs.

faq.q: How do I read tire size markings for the calculator?
faq.a: Tire size format is width/aspect ratio/rim diameter. For example, 225/60R16 means 225mm width, 60% aspect ratio (sidewall height), and 16-inch rim diameter. Enter these values in our tire calculator for accurate comparisons.

faq.q: Can tire size changes affect my vehicle's warranty?
faq.a: Significant tire size changes may affect warranty coverage, especially for drivetrain components. Consult your vehicle manufacturer and stay within recommended tire size ranges to maintain warranty protection.
